title: Whipped running stitch
subtitle: A raised corded line built by whipping a second thread over a running stitch base
excerpt: Whipped running stitch layers two passes over the same line. The first pass lays a row of running stitches; the second threads a contrasting or matching thread over and under each stitch without piercing the fabric. The result is a smooth, corded outline with more weight than plain running stitch.
sourceNotes: Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), running and whipping stitches section (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: The drawn or traced line on the fabric that guides where the stitches go.

content.text: Whipped running stitch is a two-pass line stitch from the running stitch family. A foundation row of evenly spaced running stitches is laid along a

; a second thread is then whipped (looped) over and under each stitch without entering the fabric again. The whipping gives the line a corded, rope-like quality. It appears in crewelwork borders, monogram outlines and any design that calls for a firm, raised line.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands for the running base; 2 strands (same or contrasting colour) for the whipping

items.label: Needle
items.value: Embroidery needle size 7 or 8 for the base pass; blunt tapestry needle size 24 for the whipping pass

content.text: Secure the thread on the back and bring the needle up at point A, at the start of the line.

Insert the needle down at point B, roughly 3 mm along the line. Come back up at point C, another 3 mm further on. This makes one running stitch with a 3 mm gap between it and the next. Keep stitches and gaps as equal as you can.
Continue in the same rhythm to the end of the line. Fasten off the base thread on the back.

Thread the tapestry needle with the whipping thread. Bring it up at the very start of the line, just beside the first running stitch. Slide the needle under the first stitch from right to left, without catching the fabric.

Move to the next running stitch and slide the needle under it in the same direction (right to left). Keep the tension gentle so the whipping sits over the base stitches without pulling them out of line.
Continue whipping each stitch to the end of the row. Take the needle to the back beside the last stitch and fasten off.

attrs.heading: When whipped running stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: The whipping thread catches the fabric
items.cause: Using a sharp needle for the whipping pass
items.fix: Switch to a blunt tapestry needle for the whipping pass. It slides under the base stitches without splitting the fabric threads.

items.symptom: The line looks uneven and lumpy
items.cause: Unequal base stitches, or the whipping pulled too tight
items.fix: Keep base stitches and gaps the same length. When whipping, let the thread lie naturally over the base rather than pulling it snug.
